title: After an uncertain errand, the travelers are told not to worry
setting: The church carried heavy debts from building the Kirtland temple and buying land in Ohio and Missouri. In late July 1836, Joseph Smith, Hyrum Smith, Oliver Cowdery, and Sidney Rigdon traveled east, staying in Salem, Massachusetts, from 5 August. The official heading says they had heard that a large sum of money might be available there. No contemporary record states their reasons, and no money came of the trip. The revelation is dated 6 August 1836.
summary: The revelation says the Lord is “not displeased” with the journey, despite their “follies”. It says there is much treasure in Salem for Zion, and people to gather in due time. It tells them to form acquaintances with men in the city. It promises the city and its gold and silver will be theirs in due time. It tells them not to worry about their debts or about Zion. They should stay in the area, and the Spirit’s peace will show where. They are to inquire about the city’s early inhabitants and founders. It ends with counsel to be “wise as serpents” and a promise to “order all things for your good”.

contextNote.title: Correction without condemnation
contextNote.text: The men had come east under pressure from debt, with uncertain hopes. Verse 1 opens by naming their “follies” but says the Lord is not displeased. Verses 5–6 lift two burdens: their debts and their worry for Zion. Verse 10 says there are “more treasures than one” in the city. Verse 11 then asks them to be wise yet “without sin”. It promises to order things “as fast as ye are able to receive them”. In this passage, the Lord’s ordering is gradual and fits what they can receive.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 111–114 takes its title, “I Will Order All Things for Your Good,” from verse 11. What might “more treasures than one” in verse 10 have meant for these men?
reviewNote: Read all 11 verses. Official heading gives Salem, Massachusetts, 6 August 1836, the four travelers, temple debts, and a reported sum of money. JSP introduction read: no contemporary source gives the reasons; later accounts (Brewster 1843, Robinson 1889) tie it to hidden money; the group arrived 5 August and visited New York City and Boston. Original manuscript lost; canonized text follows W. W. Phelps’s copy.
